svg.title: Tools are the load-bearing layer; resources and prompts are additive
svg.desc: Three stacked layers describe the server. The top two are drawn with dashed outlines and each carries a dashed chip reading additive: prompts.py, marked patchy support, holding onboard_engineer, incident_playbook and explain_topic, with a note that a client without prompts loses three shortcuts and nothing else because each prompt is a sequence of tool calls the model could have made itself; and resources.py, marked common support, holding the URIs knowledge index, knowledge doc by slug, and knowledge section by slug and anchor. The bottom layer, tools.py, is drawn solid and filled in the accent colour, marked universal and load-bearing and chipped the floor, holding search_docs, get_doc and list_topics. Three arrows run down from the resources layer into the floor, beside the claim that every URI is reachable through a tool byte for byte and that a test walks resources/list and asserts it. The prompts mapping runs out to a rail beside the stack, down past the resources layer, and turns back in through the right edge of the floor, so every arrow in the figure ends inside the tools box. A panel on the right, headed the mapping is asserted rather than documented, names two tests: one that walks resources/list and asserts that some tool call returns byte-identical text for every URI, failing with the URI named when a resource has no tool path, and one that answers a real handbook question using nothing but tools/list and tools/call, which is what the least capable host sees. A closing line says that removing the floor breaks everything, that removing either layer above it only makes the same corpus less convenient to reach, and that building it the other way round makes the server silently do less on some hosts.
svg.text: Put the capability in a tool. Let richer clients present it better.
Every arrow points down. Nothing above the floor holds capability of its own.
A client without prompts loses three shortcuts. Nothing else.
Each is a sequence of tool calls the model could have made itself.
Every URI is reachable through a tool, byte for byte.
A test walks resources/list and asserts it.
The mapping is asserted, not documented
